extraction.note: The problem's third line of attack (structure outside the gauge quantum numbers that sees the neutral singlets). The stored ladder tested only the Standard Model gauge algebra, u(5) and so(10); the intermediate algebras, among them the Pati-Salam stage of the stored chain, were not tested. Result: a dichotomy. Hypercharge grades so(10) with disjoint eigenvalue sets on u(5) and on the pair-creation and pair-annihilation parts, so any algebra containing the Standard Model either lies in u(5), and then the vacuum-swapped halving commutes with it, or contains one pair-creation element and its adjoint, and then that pair alone, with the stored anomaly-free charged chirality, fixes the halving to (-1)^N up to the overall label, without number conservation. Pati-Salam (the split-preserving 21), left-right, su(4) x su(2)_L x u(1) and flipped u(5) decide the bit; Georgi-Glashow u(5), and the Standard Model with B - L or with the total mode number, do not. Two further sightings: the stored Yukawa pairing (the 10, 120 and 126 forms are odd-grade Clifford elements) couples the swapped half's neutral singlet to nothing else in its half, so the rung coupling then gives no Dirac neutrino coupling (only a grade-four element links it to the lepton doublet); and the Clifford CPT antiunitary (a Majorana product times complex conjugation, the five-mode analogue of the stored pseudoscalar-rotor form) commutes with the swap and reverses both candidates, so it is blind to the bit. Reading: the grading clause is equivalent, given the other clauses, to the chirality commuting with any gauge algebra that leaves u(5), for instance the Pati-Salam algebra of the stored chain; since the chain is itself stated under (S), this is an exchange of the clause for structure the series registers, not a derivation of it. See \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}: the light-ray array count is sixteen per generation for every halving, so the light-ray chirality channels are blind to the bit. See \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square} and synthesis.up-down-split-under-conjugate-reading-needs-su2r-odd-weighting: their Dirac-neutrino clauses use the halving (-1)^N that (iii) shows the Pati-Salam stage forces. In the restated slot-module premise the grading clause reads: the chirality commutes with the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain; by (iii), given the other clauses, that form and the grading form are equivalent. Transport-absent in content (finite Clifford algebra on the series' module).

levels.formal:
Let $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ be the five-mode module of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, modes $1, 2$ the slots and $3, 4, 5$ the pairs, $N$ the total mode number, $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$, $\Omega$ the empty and $\Omega^{\top}$ the full state. Let $\so(10)$ be the span of all bilinears, $\uu(5)$ that of the number-conserving ones $a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$, and $\mathfrak{p}$ that of the pair-creation and pair-annihilation bilinears $a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}$, $a_{i}a_{j}$, so $\so(10) = \uu(5) \oplus \mathfrak{p}$. Let $\Gamma' = (-1)^{N} - 2P_{\Omega} + 2P_{\Omega^{\top}}$ be the vacuum-swapped halving of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}, and call a gauge-commuting CPT halving anomaly-free when it agrees with $\pm(-1)^{N}$ on the charged states (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Hypercharge grading.)} $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is diagonal on the bilinear basis with eigenvalues $\{0, \pm\tfrac56\}$ on $\uu(5)$, $\{1, \tfrac16, -\tfrac23\}$ on pair creation and $\{-1, -\tfrac16, \tfrac23\}$ on pair annihilation, three disjoint sets. Hence every subspace $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \so(10)$ stable under $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is $(\mathfrak{g} \cap \uu(5)) \oplus (\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p})$, and $\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p}$ is spanned by pure creation and pure annihilation elements.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One pair decides.)} $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with $\so(10)$; $\Gamma'$ commutes with $\uu(5)$, and $x \mapsto [\Gamma', x]$ is injective on $\mathfrak{p}$. For an involution equal to $s(-1)^{N}$ ($s = \pm1$) on the charged states and arbitrary on the neutral block, commuting with one nonzero pure creation element $x \in \mathfrak{p}$ forces $\Gamma\Omega^{\top} = -s\Omega^{\top}$ and $\Gamma\Omega \in s\Omega + \C\Omega^{\top}$, and commuting with $x$ and $x^{\dagger}$ forces $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Dichotomy.)} Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be closed under adjoints with $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)) \subseteq \mathfrak{g} \subseteq \so(10)$. If $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \uu(5)$, the vacuum-swapped halving commutes with $\mathfrak{g}$ and the bit is free. If $\mathfrak{g} \not\subseteq \uu(5)$, the anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halvings that commute with $\mathfrak{g}$ are exactly $\pm(-1)^{N}$, with no use of number conservation or of the grading clause. In particular the Pati-Salam algebra $\so(4) \oplus \so(6)$ of the split-preserving bivectors (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}), the left-right algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \su(2)_{R} \oplus \uu(1)_{B - L}$, $\su(4) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)$ and the flipped $\uu(5)$ fix the bit; the Georgi-Glashow $\uu(5)$, and the Standard Model algebra with $B - L$ or with $N$ adjoined, do not.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Yukawa forms.)} With the invariant pairing $B$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes}: for $(-1)^{N}$ the slot vectors pair the lepton doublet (one slot, three pairs) with $\Omega$; for $\Gamma'$ the full state $\Omega^{\top}$ has $B(\Omega^{\top}, X\psi) = B(\psi, X\Omega^{\top}) = 0$ for every other state $\psi$ of its half and every Clifford element $X$ of grade $1$, $3$ or $5$, keeps a nonzero self-pairing $B(\Omega^{\top}, X\Omega^{\top})$, and meets the lepton doublet only through grade four. The charged states of the two halves coincide. Hence, for Yukawa couplings that are odd-grade forms $B(\psi, X\varphi)$ (the $10$, $120$ and $126$ forms of the stored mass relations; under $\Gamma'$ the particle half is not an $\so(10)$ module, so these forms are an assumption there, not singled out), the rung coupling gives the particle half's neutral singlet a Dirac coupling to the lepton doublet under $(-1)^{N}$ and none under $\Gamma'$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(CPT blindness.)} $\Theta = U\kappa$, with $U = \prod_{k}(a^{\dagger}_{k} + a_{k})$ and $\kappa$ complex conjugation in the occupation basis (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors; $\kappa$ sends $I_{4}$ to $-I_{4}$), commutes with all ten Hermitian Majoranas, so with $\Spin(10)$, carries $\Omega$ to $\pm\Omega^{\top}$, commutes with the swap $S$ of $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$, and satisfies $\Theta(-1)^{N}\Theta^{-1} = -(-1)^{N}$ and $\Theta\Gamma'\Theta^{-1} = -\Gamma'$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, given the other clauses of the slot-module hypothesis (\claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}) and anomaly freedom, the grading form of its chirality clause (its earlier version) is equivalent to the chirality commuting with some gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ that leaves $\uu(5)$, the Pati-Salam algebra of the chain among them (the clause's current form), and is not implied by any that stays inside it.
levels.technical: The stored ladder showed that symmetry, CPT and anomaly freedom leave one binary choice in the composite's chirality, whether the empty or the full five-mode state is the particle half's sterile singlet, and that only operators of $\so(10)$ that create or destroy two modes see it. This result asks which gauge algebras between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ contain such operators. Hypercharge sorts $\so(10)$ into three eigenvalue families that never overlap (number-conserving, pair-creating, pair-annihilating), so any gauge algebra containing hypercharge either stays entirely inside the number-conserving $\uu(5)$ or contains a pair-creation operator and its adjoint. One such pair, with the anomaly-fixed signs on the charged states, already pins the neutral block, and number conservation is not needed. So the Pati-Salam, left-right and flipped stages decide the bit and the Georgi-Glashow stage cannot. Two cross-checks: under the swapped choice the stored Yukawa forms (all of odd Clifford grade) leave the particle half's singlet uncoupled from the rest of the half, so the rung coupling gives no Dirac neutrino coupling; and the Clifford CPT antiunitary treats both choices alike. Since the stored chain, stated under (S), runs through Pati-Salam, the clause can be read as the chirality commuting with the chain's intermediate gauge algebra: an exchange of premises onto registered structure, not a derivation from nothing.
levels.lay: Each matter particle of one family is a pattern of five filled or empty slots, and one yes-or-no choice in sorting patterns into particles and antiparticles had been left as an assumption: whether the completely empty pattern goes with the particles. This result shows which larger symmetries can settle that choice. Any symmetry that can create or remove two slots at once settles it, and the symmetries that only move slots around never do. The intermediate symmetry stage the series already uses, Pati-Salam, is of the first kind, so if the sorting respects that symmetry, the choice is fixed; this trades the assumption for that requirement rather than removing it. With the other choice, and mass couplings of the usual kind, the neutrino partner would have no ordinary mass coupling to the rest of its family.
levels.one-liner: $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ separates $\so(10)$ into $\uu(5)$ and pair creation and annihilation with disjoint eigenvalues, so a gauge algebra between the Standard Model and $\so(10)$ either lies in $\uu(5)$, leaving the neutral-singlet bit free, or contains one pair bilinear and its adjoint, which with the anomaly-fixed charged chirality forces $\pm(-1)^{N}$: Pati-Salam, left-right and flipped stages decide the bit, Georgi-Glashow does not; under the swapped choice the singlet has no odd-grade Yukawa pairing in its half, and the Clifford CPT antiunitary is blind to the bit.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} On the five-mode module of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}, with $Y = \sum_{k} y_{k} n_{k}$, $y_{k} = \tfrac12$ on the slots and $-\tfrac13$ on the pairs, $[Y, a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}] = (y_{i} - y_{j})a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$, $[Y, a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}] = (y_{i} + y_{j})a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}$ and $[Y, a_{i}a_{j}] = -(y_{i} + y_{j})a_{i}a_{j}$. The differences $y_{i} - y_{j}$ are $0$ and $\pm\tfrac56$; the sums $y_{i} + y_{j}$ are $1$ (two slots), $\tfrac16$ (slot and pair) and $-\tfrac23$ (two pairs). The three sets $\{0, \pm\tfrac56\}$, $\{1, \tfrac16, -\tfrac23\}$, $\{-1, -\tfrac16, \tfrac23\}$ are disjoint, so each eigenspace of $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ on $\so(10)$ lies in $\uu(5)$, in the creation span or in the annihilation span. A subspace stable under $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$ is the sum of its intersections with the eigenspaces, which gives the splitting. The check verifies every eigenvalue equation on the $45$ basis elements and the disjointness.

\emph{(ii).} Every bilinear changes $N$ by an even amount, so $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with $\so(10)$, and $\Gamma'$, which differs from it only by the projectors onto $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$ (both annihilated by every $a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$ with $i \ne j$ and eigenvectors of every $n_{i}$), commutes with $\uu(5)$. Write an involution as $s(-1)^{N}$ on the thirty charged states and $\Gamma\Omega = a\Omega + c\Omega^{\top}$, $\Gamma\Omega^{\top} = b\Omega + d\Omega^{\top}$. Let $x = \sum_{i<j} c_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j} \ne 0$ and pick $c_{ij} \ne 0$. Then $x\Omega$ is a nonzero charged state of degree two, $x\Omega^{\top} = 0$, so $[\Gamma, x]\Omega = s\,x\Omega - a\,x\Omega$ gives $a = s$. For $\varphi$ the degree-three state on the complement of $\{i, j\}$, $x\varphi = \pm c_{ij}\Omega^{\top}$ and $\Gamma x\varphi = \pm c_{ij}(b\Omega + d\Omega^{\top})$, while $x\Gamma\varphi = -s\,x\varphi$ has no $\Omega$ component; so $b = 0$ and $d = -s$. The entry $c$ is not constrained by $x$ (the involution with $c = 1$ commutes with the Standard Model and with $x$; checked). For $x^{\dagger}$, a pure annihilation element, $x^{\dagger}\Omega = 0$ and $x^{\dagger}\Omega^{\top} \ne 0$ is charged, so $[\Gamma, x^{\dagger}]\Omega = -c\,x^{\dagger}\Omega^{\top}$ gives $c = 0$. Hence $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$. Injectivity: for $x$ a nonzero creation element, $[\Gamma', x]\Omega = (+1 - (-1))x\Omega = 2x\Omega \ne 0$, and $x \mapsto x\Omega = \sum c_{ij}e_{i} \wedge e_{j}$ is injective; for annihilation elements use $\Omega^{\top}$; the creation and annihilation images lie in different degrees. The check solves the affine system for $(a, b, c, d)$ for every one of the ten basis pairs $x, x^{\dagger}$ and both $s$, finds rank $4$ with the solution $(s, 0, 0, -s)$, rank $3$ for $x$ alone, rank $2$ with $N$ in place of $x$ (diagonal block), rank $0$ for the Standard Model alone, and rank $20$ for the twenty columns of $[\Gamma', \cdot]$.

\emph{(iii).} The Standard Model algebra contains $Y$, so $\mathfrak{g}$ is $\mathrm{ad}\,Y$-stable and splits by (i). If $\mathfrak{g} \subseteq \uu(5)$, $\Gamma'$ commutes with it by (ii), and so does $-\Gamma'$; both are anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halvings (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(ii)), so the bit is not fixed. If not, $\mathfrak{g} \cap \mathfrak{p}$ is nonzero and spanned by pure creation and pure annihilation eigenvectors; closure under adjoints (a gauge algebra is the complexification of a compact real form, so it is closed under $x \mapsto x^{\dagger}$) supplies $x$ and $x^{\dagger}$ with $x$ pure creation. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4) an anomaly-free gauge-commuting CPT halving is $s(-1)^{N}$ on the charged states, and by (ii) commuting with $x, x^{\dagger}$ forces $\Gamma = s(-1)^{N}$, which does commute with $\mathfrak{g}$. The named algebras: Pati-Salam is the span of the slot bilinears ($\so(4)$, including $a^{\dagger}_{1}a^{\dagger}_{2}$) and the pair bilinears ($\so(6)$, including $a^{\dagger}_{3}a^{\dagger}_{4}$), the $21$ split-preserving bivectors of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}; the left-right algebra contains $\su(2)_{R} \ni a^{\dagger}_{1}a^{\dagger}_{2}$; $\su(4)$ contains the pair-pair brackets; the flipped $\uu(5)$ (number-conserving for the modes with the two slots' creation and annihilation exchanged) contains the slot-pair brackets $a_{i}a_{j}$, $a^{\dagger}_{j}a^{\dagger}_{i}$. The check verifies, for each named algebra, membership of $Y$, whether it lies in $\uu(5)$ (a span computation), that $(-1)^{N}$ commutes with it, that $\Gamma'$ commutes with it exactly when it lies in $\uu(5)$, and the neutral-block solution ($(1, 0, 0, -1)$ at rank $4$ for those leaving $\uu(5)$, rank below $4$ otherwise). $B - L$ is taken up to a central constant, $-k/3$, which does not change any commutator.

\emph{(iv).} The pairing $B$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes} pairs the state on a mode set $S$ only with the state on the complement, so $B(\psi, X\varphi) \ne 0$ needs $N(\psi) + N(X\varphi) = 5$. A Clifford monomial of grade $r$ changes $N$ by an amount of the parity of $r$. For $\psi = \Omega^{\top}$ ($N = 5$) and $\varphi$ a charged state of $\Gamma'$'s particle half ($N$ even), $X\varphi$ must be $\Omega$, impossible for odd $r$; the same for $B(\varphi, X\Omega^{\top})$ ($N(X\Omega^{\top})$ even, needs $N = 5 - N(\varphi)$ odd). For $r$ odd, $X\Omega^{\top}$ can be $\Omega$ (the product of the five annihilations has grade-five and lower odd components), which gives the self-pairing. The lepton doublet ($N = 4$) pairs with $\Omega^{\top}$ only if $N(X\Omega^{\top}) = 1$, a change of $-4$, even grade; with $(-1)^{N}$ it pairs with $\Omega$ through a slot vector ($N(X\Omega) = 1$). The check computes $B$ from the stored construction, confirms its invariance in this labelling of the modes, and evaluates all $382$ monomials of grades $1$, $3$, $5$ and the $210$ of grade $4$ on the relevant states. The $10$, $120$ and $126$ Yukawa forms of the stored mass relations are of grades $1$, $3$, $5$; so under $\Gamma'$ the rung coupling gives the particle half's singlet no Dirac coupling to the lepton doublet.

\emph{(v).} $U$ is a product of five mutually anticommuting real Majoranas, so it commutes with each of them and anticommutes with each $a^{\dagger}_{k} - a_{k}$; $\kappa$ fixes the real matrices and negates $I_{4}(a^{\dagger}_{k} - a_{k})$; so $\Theta$ fixes all ten Hermitian Majoranas and hence their bivectors. $U\Omega$ is the product of five creations on $\Omega$ up to sign, i.e. $\pm\Omega^{\top}$; $U$ is real, maps degree $d$ to degree $5 - d$ on each mode, so it reverses $(-1)^{N}$, exchanges $\Omega$ and $\Omega^{\top}$ and therefore commutes with $S$ and reverses $\Gamma' = S(-1)^{N}S$. All verified exactly.

The closing equivalence: by (iii) any gauge algebra leaving $\uu(5)$ forces $\pm(-1)^{N}$, which is the grading clause (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(iii)); conversely $\pm(-1)^{N}$ commutes with all of $\so(10)$; and an algebra inside $\uu(5)$ leaves the vacuum-swapped halving. Numerical work: none; all statements are exact.
